Land Use by Neighborhood
Alma CNRA:
The Alma neighborhood is a basically residential area which has experienced intrusions of commercial and light industrial uses. The entire easterly boundary of Alma is strip commercial along Monterey Highway. San Jose Avenue, which forms the southerly boundary, has a mixture of commercial and light industrial uses, some on the site of converted single-family residences. More commercial sites occur on Alma Avenue near the northwesterly corner of the neighborhood. The railroad spur line which passes through the southerly part of Alma parallel to San Jose Avenue has been an influencing factor in the spread of light industrial uses in the area.
Alviso CNRA:
The Alviso Planning Area is largely devoid of urban development, being mostly devoted to agriculture and open space uses. The City's General Plan, however, shows much of the area as planned for future industrial and residential uses. At present the community area of Alviso consists of small areas of homes, with scattered commercial uses, and some light industrial uses, generally related to the waterfront location of Alviso.
Campus CNRA:
The Campus neighborhood has two perimeters of solid commercial uses: Santa Clara Street, the northerly boundary and 4th Street, the westerly boundary. Further commercial uses, generally food service outlets, are located along the northerly side of San Fernando Street, the project area's southerly perimeter. Across this street outside the CNRA is the campus of San Jose State University. The largest commercial concentration is along Santa Clara Street between 5th and 6th Streets; a neighborhood commercial shopping center dominated by a large supermarket. The remainder of the Campus area is primarily multifamily dwelling units, generally housing the elderly and students. In many cases, large older houses have been converted to apartments for this reason. There also exist several relatively modern apartment buildings constructed specifically for the college-aged population. A large religious institution, complete with parking facility, is located on 6th Street, near San Fernando. This building is owned and operated by the Church of Jesus Christ of the Latter Day Saints. Another religious-operated building is at the corner of San Fernando and 5th Streets. The Catholic Womens Center, which houses the John XXIII Senior Center and the adjacent Newman Center are owned and operated by the Roman Catholic Church. The Senior Center is the site of one CDBG project involving the rehabilitation of existing building areas.
